Alex: Heads up — ran into a reproducible perf cliff on Mistral-8x7B when a request crosses max_position_embeddings boundary with our adaptive batcher. Repro below, pretty noisy but consistent :grimacing:
Maya: ack, do you think it's kernel selection flipping or KV cache bookkeeping?
Alex: profiling suggests both. quick dump:
```
# perf summary (p95 windows around boundary)
kv_tile_split        40.3%
memcpy_async         18.7%  (spikes at seq_len = 1025..1030)
fast_attn_kernel     15.1%
fallback_attn_kernel 20.9%  (triggered when pos_index > model.max_pos)
```
Jordan: hmm that fallback jump looks like kernel chooser sees pos wrap and loses the optimized path. Could be RoPE scaling clamp or a mask build path that touches different kernel.
Sam: I noticed earlier our batcher will try to merge sequences that push effective token index over max_pos instead of splitting. That can create a tiny sub-batch with seq_len ~ max_pos+N which trips the kernel guard.
Maya: can you paste minimal repro?
Alex: yup, small script:
```bash
python -c "from infra.tests import replay; replay.run(model='mistral-8x7b', seq_a=1000, seq_b=40)"
# run with non-deterministic batching on canary shard
```
Jordan: also check RoPE scale config. If we quantize or use a shim scaling factor for 8x7B, the chooser logic comparing max_pos against requested pos might be off-by-one. We had a recent change to apply a scale factor at kernel/runtime boundary.
Sam: reproduced locally on gpusim. When seq boundary crosses 1024->1026 we see the memcpy spike and kernel switch. When I forcibly clamp seq to <=1024,perf is back to stable.
Alex: tentative root cause: (a) batcher merges two requests and creates a virtual position > max_pos, (b) mask builder computes the attention mask using 32-bit indices, which overflows wrap vs RoPE expectation, (c) kernel selector sees mask/pos mismatch and switches to generic fallback that copies KV tiles into a different layout -> memcpy thrash.
Maya: good triage. Proposed fixes: 1) Add a batcher guard to avoid merging across max_pos boundary, 2) Add kernel-chooser unit test for poswrap, 3) Harden mask builder types (use 64-bit) and add quick path to prefer fast_attn for small overflow windows.
Jordan: agree. For (1) we can implement a cheap heuristic: if max(seq_lengths) + min(seq_start_offsets) > model.max_pos => split. Should be low perf overhead.
Sam: I'll prototype patch. Also we should add a micro-benchmark to detect memcpy spikes. Patch plan:
- batcher: refuse merge across boundary (sam/PR)
- runtime: add kernel-chooser fallback sanity check (maya/PR)
- tests: add replay scenarios and perf assertion (jordan/PR)
Alex: timeline? This is causing ~12% p99 latency regression on canaries for some workloads.
Sam: prototype PR by EOD, unit tests next day. Canary rollout to a small pool initially.
Maya: one more: add a telemetry counter for "poswrap_kernel_switch" so we can alert if we see >0 in prod.
deploy-bot: Canary rollout scheduled: mistral8x7b-poswrap-guard -> pool:canary-small at 2026-03-18T14:42Z
Alex: thanks — will follow up with perf graphs after canary. If it passes we merge and then backport to M7B branch. :thumbsup:
Jordan: also add a note in the release checklist: "watch for poswrap kernel chooser excursions"
Sam: ack. I'll link the PR here once open.
Maya: great work, short-term guard + telemetry looks low risk.
Alex: closing loop — next steps tracked in #eng-releases ticket 4521.
